### 2026-07-19 - Codex - top-row tool quality gauntlet

- Owner authorizes an extended live-use pass over SELECT, RETOUCH, MASK, TRANSFORM and ADJUST, including removing or replacing tools that do not earn their place for car-livery, spec-map and UV-template editing. Claimed the bounded SPB-93 tool lane.
- **Live inventory / baseline:** exercised representative top-row paths on the real imported PSD. Clone source + stroke + one-step undo and existing Color Replace's target/replacement/tolerance/all-Layers workflow were useful and behaved coherently. The Transform menu's `Transform Decal` was a permanent zombie: no active producer exists for `selectedDecalIndex` / `decalLayers`. Brightness/Contrast and Hue/Saturation exposed sliders but did not show their effect until Apply, making judgment blind and un-Photoshop-like.
- **Pass 153 - Fit Layer to Zone Selection:** replaced Transform Decal with an SPB-native artwork-placement bridge. Pure `js/canvas/layer/selection-placement.js` computes bounded proportional fit geometry only. The controller reads the active Zone selection without mutating it, fits the selected editable PSD Layer with 6% breathing room, and delegates preview/Enter/Escape/history/raster ownership to the existing Layer transform system. Starting the command explicitly clears the one-shot Pick Item bbox so a stale glyph cannot hijack a whole-Layer fit.
- **Pass 153 served proof:** on real PSD Layer `Numbers`, the command opened a **347×643 px** aspect-locked fit preview inside the active Zone selection. Escape hid the transform bar without history; Apply returned `Layer transform applied`; unified Ctrl+Z returned `Undid layer: free transform`. No Zone mask was written.
- **Pass 154 - true live Adjust candidates:** added pure `js/canvas/layer/adjustment-preview.js` and routed both live and immediate Brightness/Contrast + Hue/Saturation/Lightness through the same alpha-preserving RGBA math. Each modal captures one immutable source, rAF-throttles slider candidates, clips the candidate to the active selection, and publishes no history. Cancel restores the exact source. Apply first restores the source and then calls the existing transactional commit, guaranteeing exactly one truthful undo instead of snapshotting preview pixels.
- **Pass 154 served proof:** Brightness changed its readout from 0 to +35 during preview while the Zone history remained untouched; Cancel closed with no transaction. Reopen + Apply produced `Brightness +35, Contrast 0`; unified Undo returned `Undid layer: brightness / contrast`. Hue +45° / Saturation +25 previewed and Cancel left the next Undo at `Nothing to undo`. Both dialogs expose the live-preview/cancel contract and retain Enter/Escape. Browser console errors: **0**.
- **Performance / verification:** 2048² pure-kernel probe measured **26.5 ms Brightness/Contrast** and **61.4 ms Hue/Saturation**. Root + Electron module/canvas syntax and manifest JSON are clean. Focused placement, preview, adjustment transaction, feathered selection, dialog, wrapper-parity and alpha-safety lanes pass **22/22**. Runtime write+verify synchronized the intended writable files; HTML, canvas and both new modules are byte-identical across root/Electron. The standing **22 report-only Smart TGA/engine drifts** were left untouched.
- **Documentation / handoff:** `docs/TOOL_ARCHITECTURE.md` records both pure-module ownership boundaries and `CHANGELOG.md` records the user-visible behavior. The required single Linear SPB-93 read returned `reauthentication_required`; per the low-usage protocol there was no retry churn. This Living Wiki entry is the authoritative handoff until the Linear connection is renewed.

### 2026-07-19 - Codex - Easy SPEC SCULPT multi-color + linked scale

- Audit found **two different customer-facing Easy Spec Sculpt implementations**. - Browser QA on a real exact-2048 Chevy Truck PSD uncovered and fixed a dangerous flex layout bug: the shrinking library let look cards overflow underneath the install panel. The rail now gives the library non-shrinking flow ownership and places the install box before it, so no controls share pixels. A patterned `Brushed Metal Fine` preview produced different hashes at 1.00x vs 0.50x (`8F6E98C892F08194` vs `66466E4499E9C30E`). The canonical original-lab button navigated to Easy while the lab retained Shokk the World, Auto-Sculpt and Advanced. Focused syntax/compile + Easy/beta tests are **8/8 green**.
- Final root -> `electron-app/server` write/verify is clean for every writable runtime asset; SHA-256 pairs match for server, Easy JS/CSS, original lab, main boot/HTML and the new engine helper. The only dry-run output is the existing **22 report-only** Smart-TGA/engine/model drifts, untouched. Browser QA tabs and the isolated port-59877 server were closed. ### 2026-07-16 - Codex - `.shokk` save/recall diagnosis started

- Owner reports another customer's left-menu `SAVE SHOKK` package may not appear or reload even though the owner's own files load. Tracing the exact per-user Windows library path, what spec/paint/session data is actually packaged, and the complete list/open/hydration chain before proposing a fix.
- Scope is read-only diagnosis plus Wiki coordination. No customer files will be moved/deleted and no renderer, finish, Forge, Smart TGA, or painting-tool code is in this lane.
- Exact location is `C:\Users\<Windows user>\Documents\Shokker Paint Booth\SHOKK Library`. The app exposes this exact path in the LOAD SHOKK modal and its `Folder` button. A baked spec is stored as `spec.png` *inside* the `.shokk` ZIP archive, not as a loose neighboring file; library recall scans only this user folder plus bundled factory presets.
- Local evidence rules out generic version incompatibility: all **25/25** owner archives opened and parsed, spanning manifest SPB versions **5.0.0, 5.9.0, 7.0.9, and 8.0.3-beta**. However, only **15/25 contain a spec**; **10/25 are valid session packages with no `spec.png`**. Those restore zones/recipe but cannot perform `Spec Map Only` recall.
- Root UX defect: SAVE SHOKK is allowed before a successful current render. It still reports success, with `No spec (render first)` only inside a transient toast. Server selection uses `lastRenderedJobId` when available, then `_latest_render`, then the newest job; therefore a no-render save can contain no spec or an older fallback rather than the intended current map. The customer's first discriminator is whether the library card says `✓ Spec`.
- Machine-specific path trap: Python builds a literal `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\...` path rather than resolving Windows' Known Documents folder. On OneDrive-redirected machines the customer may be searching under `OneDrive\Documents` while SPB created/uses the non-OneDrive folder. A moved/downloaded `.shokk` outside the exact library folder is not listed.
- No production code changed. To determine this customer's exact branch, request: screenshot of the SAVE result/library card, the path printed in the modal, app version, and the `.shokk` file. The package alone proves immediately whether `spec.png` is missing or corrupt; if it contains a spec, next evidence is the exact red failure toast/log.

### 2026-07-16 - Codex - natural Base / Color / Spec controls (DONE)

- **Owner contract:** Base Strength 0 must always equal untouched source paint regardless of selected base or chosen color; intermediate values must be a smooth source-to-result interpolation. Color Strength must independently fade only the chosen color contribution. Spec Scale must follow Base Scale by default, with an explicit independent override.
- **Root cause repaired:** regular `compose_paint_mod`, stacked composition, and the three monolithic render paths had two competing Base Strength mechanisms: renderer inputs were weakened and the intermediate result was blended toward an underpaint/color substrate. Because the final chosen-color override happened outside that envelope, 0 could remain pink/green/black. Each path now renders its full base/material/color/HSB result first and then applies one literal `source * (1-strength) + result * strength` mix before separate patterns. Monolithics also no longer receive partial chosen color in their underpaint and again afterward; Color Strength is one independent post-material fade, including for underpaint-sensitive finishes.
- **Scale-link contract:** added Node-testable `js/zones/base-spec-scale-link.js`. Missing mode now means linked; moving Base Scale updates Base + Spec atomically; an unchecked `Independent Spec` checkbox disables the Spec controls; checking it starts from the current Base value and permits divergence; unchecking immediately re-links. `specScaleMode` and the resolved value now survive live config and Finish DNA round trips, including the still-active giant-state persistence paths.
- **Proof:** new natural-control suite + monolithic regression **7/7**. A wider source/scale/config/DNA sweep was **56/57**; the lone failure is the older `cx_arctic` scale test expecting base paint art in source mode, already contradicted by the July 8 owner contract that source mode preserves original colors, and Base Strength 1 is behaviorally unchanged by this patch. Served Pro UI verified Base 0.35 -> disabled Spec 0.35, explicit Spec 0.80 surviving Base 0.50, uncheck -> Spec 0.50, and Base/Color Strength endpoint labels 0/100; all test state restored. Root -> Electron sync wrote/verified all changed runtime pairs; the existing 22 Smart TGA/report-only drifts remain untouched. Native installed shell launched, but Windows activation and passive capture both failed at the OS interface (`0x80004002`), so no native interaction claim is made.

- Cycle 367 completed the route-RGB follow-up for Cycle 366's tiny warm speckled livery fleck near-misses. The important diagnostic was that the live `/api/auto-layers` route RGB is not the same pixel field as the inspector display PNG: route RGB uses `load_paint_rgb_float01(... target_size=1024)` with OpenCV `INTER_LANCZOS4`, while the saved preview sheet uses PIL Lanczos, and that difference mattered on 5-7 px flecks. Real route-RGB measurement showed the remaining Mustang textless livery flecks were just below the existing universal `tiny_warm_speckled_livery_fleck` gate, not a new car-specific family: `[241,250,5,7]` had colored coverage **0.48**, and `[432,229,7,6]` / `[432,791,7,6]` had hue-red/orange **0.50**, with low sponsor/protected ring overlap. Confirmed visually (both 55s sideways, mid one upright).

- **🔍 FINDING (logged T17): multi-element UNDO is messy.** `selectConnectedLayerPixelsAtPoint` calls `pushUndo(selectedZoneIndex)` (a ZONE undo) on every pick (to build the zone mask), so a multi-element session interleaves zone-undos with the layer-transform stack-restores. Undoing the session with Ctrl+Z is NOT a clean one-undo-per-edit (the 2nd Ctrl+Z hit "reverted Zone 1 actions" and left the Numbers bbox grown / cyan 110 vs 106). SINGLE-element undo is clean (later 46/47/48); only the multi-step session undo interleaves. Forward flow is unaffected.

### 2026-06-05 (later 48) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: 🔧 ROOT FIX (6th this loop) &mdash; PICK ITEM near-miss no longer grabs the WHOLE CAR; snaps to the number's layer
- **Fixed owner complaint #1's last sharp edge: a click a few px OFF a number used to isolate the ENTIRE Car Paint body** (a 2048&sup2; whole-layer grab) instead of the number. Reproduced LIVE: Numbers active + PICK ITEM, a near-miss above a "55" isolated the whole car paint (bw/bh 2048, sourceLayerId psd_0).
- **Root cause:** `getTopmostVisibleLayerAtCanvasPoint` returned the topmost layer opaque at the EXACT click pixel. A near-miss is transparent on the thin Numbers glyph, so the top&rarr;bottom search fell through to the Car Paint BASE layer (opaque everywhere). The ring-snap in `selectConnectedLayerPixelsAtPoint` only runs AFTER a layer is chosen, so it couldn't help once the selection had already fallen through to the base.
- **Fix (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js`, 3 edits):** made the topmost search snap-aware. New helpers `_isBaseLikeLayer` (bbox &ge;55% of canvas) + `_layerHasOpaqueWithin` (ring search, bbox-pruned). The pick handler passes the SAME zoom-aware radius (`26/dispScale`) that `selectConnectedLayerPixelsAtPoint` uses, so the layer found here also has its glyph found by that function's ring-snap. Non-pick callers (no snapRadius) get the original exact-pixel result UNCHANGED.

### 2026-06-05 (later 39) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: 🔧 FIXED the stale spec-preview-on-delete bug at the ROOT (deleteLayer now forcePreviewRefresh)
- **Fixed the recurring stale-spec-preview-on-delete flagged in later 38.** Reproduced LIVE + subagent-diagnosed the root + fixed at root + verified.
- **Root cause (parallel subagent trace):** `deleteLayer` (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js:19308`) post-delete called `triggerPreviewRender()`, whose **dedup guard** (`if (hash === lastPreviewZoneHash) return`, ~line 7882) short-circuits when the layer-hash term doesn't flip. That term only flips via `_layerCompositeRevision`, bumped inside `recompositeFromLayers()` &mdash; which **early-returns when `_psdLayers.length === 0`** (deleting the LAST layer) WITHOUT bumping it &rarr; **no spec render fires &rarr; SPEC/COMBINED preview (right pane) stays stale permanently** until a manual Refresh. (Non-last-layer deletes DO fire the render &mdash; the stale frame there was just render latency that self-clears, which is why I sometimes saw it clear on its own.)
- **🔧 FIX (root `paint-booth-3-canvas.js:~19378`, 3-copy synced, cache-buster `spb-delete-preview-refresh-20260605r`):** `deleteLayer` now calls **`forcePreviewRefresh()`** (the Refresh button's own handler) instead of `triggerPreviewRender()` &mdash; it resets `lastPreviewZoneHash` + clears the server zone/spec caches + forces a `doPreviewRender` (**preview-only; never `doRender`/deploy** &mdash; confirmed). So the preview ALWAYS refreshes after a delete, including the last-layer case.
- **VERIFIED LIVE (instrumented + looked):** reloaded (`spb-delete-preview-refresh-20260605r` confirmed loaded), wrapped `forcePreviewRefresh` with a call-counter, created a throwaway shape, **deleted via the real UI DELETE button** &rarr; `fprCalledOnDelete = 1` (the fix fires) &rarr; the SPEC/COMBINED preview **auto-refreshed and cleared the shape WITHOUT any manual Refresh click** (stale frame at +3s was the forced server render in progress; clean by ~+8s). Previously the delete left it stale (last-layer = permanently).
- **Livery PRISTINE:** count 11, 0 magenta, cyan 106 baseline, neutral (Eyedropper).
- **Note:** the render LATENCY (the spec is a ~5-8s server render) is inherent &mdash; the fix ensures the render always FIRES + completes (no manual Refresh needed), which was the actual bug. Left a harmless `forcePreviewRefresh` call-counter wrap on the live page (clears on next reload).

### 2026-06-05 (later 24) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: 🔧 FIXED ADJUST &rarr; Invert (+ Posterize) silently discarding on a layer (resolves T14) &mdash; same "preview &ne; bake" class
- **Resolved T14 (flagged last fire) &mdash; it was a REAL bug, now FIXED + verified live.** Subagent-diagnosed the root cause, applied the fix, shipped + verified.
- **Root cause:** `invertCanvasColors` (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js:24373`) inverted `paintImageData` then did `pc.getContext('2d').putImageData(...)` &mdash; updating ONLY the visible canvas. It NEVER called `_flushPaintImageDataToCurrentSurface()`, so the inverted pixels were never written into the active layer canvas (`_activeLayerCtx`). Then `_commitLayerPaint()` read the ORIGINAL (un-inverted) layer pixels + recomposite repainted them &rarr; **the invert was silently DISCARDED** (the "Colors inverted on layer" toast fired anyway). Same preview&ne;bake class as the transform clip fix (later 19). `posterize` (:24421) had the identical bug.
- **FIX:** replace the visible-canvas `putImageData` with **`_flushPaintImageDataToCurrentSurface()`** (the proven `desaturateCanvas`/`autoLevels`/`autoContrast` pattern &mdash; it flushes to the active layer surface AND updates the visible canvas AND handles the no-layer composite path) BEFORE commit. 1 line each in `invertCanvasColors` + `posterize`; defensive fallback kept; auditable comments in source.
- **SHIPPED + VERIFIED (live, post-reload):** 3-copy synced (Grep-confirmed 2 hits in each of the 3 `paint-booth-3-canvas.js`), cache-buster `paint-booth-3-canvas.js?v=`**`spb-adjust-invert-flush-20260605o`**, reloaded (11/11 layers). Re-ran the EXACT failing scenario: magenta shape (255,0,255) selected &rarr; ADJUST &rarr; Invert &rarr; **shape center is now 0,255,0 (green) and PERSISTS** (layer img + both preview panes + panel thumbnail all green). Pre-fix it stayed magenta. ✅
- **Scope:** only `invertCanvasColors` + `posterize` had the missing-flush bug (the other ADJUST tools &mdash; brightness/contrast, hue/saturation &mdash; use a separate `_getAdjustmentTarget`/`_commitAdjustment` path that's immune). Selected-layer vs paint-target can't diverge (single `_selectedLayerId`), so last fire's "wrong layer" symptom was actually this discard.

### 2026-06-05 (later 19) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: 🔧 FIXED the owner's #1 bug &mdash; per-element transform ROTATE+Apply was CLIPPING the element (now grows to the rotated AABB)
- **Found + FIXED *the* "transform doesn't half work" bug** (owner's #1). Live repro: PICK ITEM &rarr; isolate a layer &rarr; rotate **+90&deg;** &rarr; **Apply**. The element baked into a canvas sized to the ORIGINAL box, so rotated content overhanging the box was **CLIPPED**. Measured pre-fix: a 602&times;402 rect, +90&deg;, Apply &rarr; img stayed **602&times;402** (should be ~402&times;602), magenta clipped to a 402&times;402 region (left/right edges transparent). **The live PREVIEW showed the full rotation, but the BAKE lost the corners** &mdash; exactly why "prior testing" passed (preview) yet real use failed (commit). That's the owner's "despite prior testing".
- **Root cause (subagent-confirmed):** `commitLayerTransform()` whole-layer commit branch (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js` ~L21325) sized the dest canvas to `newW x newH` (original box) and drew the rotated content into it. `boxW`/`boxH` are never grown on rotation (the +90&deg; preset only sets `s.rotation`). Isolated elements (selxform, subRect=null) take this branch. (Scale-up writes the grown size to boxW/boxH so it was safe; move/scale/flip safe; only rotation clipped.)
- **FIX:** size the dest canvas to the transformed **AABB** (`newW*|cos|+newH*|sin|` &times; `newW*|sin|+newH*|cos|`), draw centered, set bbox to the AABB. **rotation===0 &rArr; AABB === newW x newH (provable identity: bx1===newX1, by1===newY1) &rArr; move/scale/flip commits byte-for-byte UNCHANGED** &mdash; only rotation grows. Full auditable comment in source.
- **SHIPPED + VERIFIED (live, post-reload):** edited root + **3-copy synced** (all 3 `paint-booth-3-canvas.js` carry the fix, Grep-confirmed), cache-buster bumped `paint-booth-3-canvas.js?v=`**`spb-rotate-apply-aabb-20260605n`**, tab reloaded (livery auto-loaded 11/11). Re-ran the exact repro: 602&times;402 rect, +90&deg;, Apply &rarr; **img now 407&times;606 (grown AABB), bbox [347,147,754,753], edge sample "MMM" (fully filled, NO clip)**; screenshot shows a proper TALL rotated rect (not clipped to a square). ✅
- **No-regression:** AABB formula is identity at rotation 0 (proven) + the +90&deg; result (407&times;606 = exact AABB) confirms the formula is geometrically correct. A no-op-apply spot-check this fire was inconclusive (an isolate-zoom/click mishap, NOT a regression); a clean real-drag move/scale spot-check is a fast optional next-fire confirmation.

Region via the zone COLOR-KEY (`colorMode='picker'` + `pickerColor` + `pickerTolerance`) / regionMask / sourceLayer. Verify via **`triggerPreviewRender()`** &mdash; never `doRender` (forbidden).

- **LIMITATION found (actionable for owner):** there is **NO window-exposed setter for the zone color-key** (`setZonePickerColor` / `setZoneColor` / `setZoneColorKey` all `undefined`). So restricting a tiling base to a specific colour region (e.g. "the yellow inside the numbers") must be done via the **UI COLOR picker**, not a one-line script. Exposed + working zone setters: `setZoneBase`, `setZoneBaseScale`, `setZonePattern`, `setZoneBaseColor`, `setZoneBaseColorSource`, `resetZoneBaseScale`, `triggerPreviewRender`, `undoZoneChange`.
- **Tiling visual = DEFERRED (de-risked):** `checkered_chrome` is a spec-driven finish (checker lives in the METALLIC channel) so the colour preview is a near-uniform wash &mdash; can't confirm tile repeats by eye there. A definitive check = a spec-channel **BEFORE/AFTER A/B** (open SPEC MAP &rarr; R Metal, apply base to a LARGE zone, look for a new checker appearing, revert). Engine tiling math IS present (`_tile_fractional`), so this is a confirmation step, not a suspected bug. Ready for a focused fire.
- **RECOVERY (clean):** reverted my 2 ops with **`window.undoZoneChange()` &times;2** (toasts "Undo: Set base scale" &rarr; "Undo: Set base: checkered_chrome"); zone 1 back to **PF: Bright Neo**, forced a "pipeline reset" refresh, render settled, **livery pristine + auto-saved**. So `applyZoom`/`canvasZoom('fit')` resize the source pane when GROWING (zoom-out&rarr;fit) but not when SHRINKING (zoom-in&rarr;fit). ### 2026-06-05 (later 4) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: isolate-zoom-IN attempted, hit a post-cancel regression, REVERTED (proper view save/restore deferred)
- **Goal:** make isolate reliably ZOOM IN on a small glyph (owner 2026-06-01: "the box came up very small and basically broke the screen") &mdash; the existing `zoomToElementForTransform` wasn't firing for the "55".
- **Root cause found:** there are TWO isolate paths. The layer-pick path (~L3300) calls `zoomToElementForTransform`; but the path that actually fires on a "click a number" pick (~L3031, toast "drag/rotate/scale only this sponsor or number") **never called it**. The zoom function itself is FINE &mdash; live diagnosis: tight bbox available (`_spbLastPickedElementBbox` 407&times;237), pane 490&times;490, it WOULD compute z=0.72; calling it manually zoomed **23%&rarr;72%** and framed the "55" beautifully.
- **Fix attempted** (token `spb-isolate-zoomin-20260605h`): wired `zoomToElementForTransform` into the firing path. **Verified live it zooms 23%&rarr;73% on a real click** &mdash; big, centered, grabbable.
- **BUT found a regression:** ending the transform (Cancel/Apply &rarr; `cancelLayerTransform` / `commitLayerTransform`) does **NOT re-fit the view**, so the source pane is left stranded at the zoomed-in scroll &mdash; **blank/desynced** (zoom indicator says 23% but `splitSource.scrollWidth` shows it's still ~73%). Cleanly reproduced post-Cancel: source pane dark. This pre-exists for the layer-pick path too; wiring zoom-in into the common path made it hit every "click a number".
- **DECISION: REVERTED** (token `spb-isolate-revert-20260605i`) &mdash; a broken-looking view after every isolate+cancel is worse than the small box, and owner doctrine is "fewer working tools &gt; many broken". The handle VISIBLE (later 3) + GRABBABLE (later 2) fixes already make the 23% box usable without zooming. **Verified after revert: isolate stays 23% + whole car visible; Cancel leaves both panes showing the full car &mdash; no desync, 0 console errors.**
- **LEFT (proper fix, next fire):** SAVE the view in `zoomToElementForTransform` (`{currentZoom, splitSource.scrollLeft/Top}`) + RESTORE on transform deactivate (`cancelLayerTransform` + `commitLayerTransform` &mdash; both live in the same closure as `currentZoom`/`applyZoom`, so the restore can `currentZoom=saved; applyZoom(); sc.scrollLeft/Top=saved`), THEN re-enable the zoom-in. Makes click&rarr;zoom-in&rarr;edit&rarr;apply/cancel&rarr;view-restored fully seamless. After that: breadth (brush / eraser / lasso / wand / recolor / gradient).

- **Owner's "transform doesn't half work" had a real, measurable cause for real-mouse users.** The per-element transform's handle grab radius was a FIXED canvas-px value (`r = 11`, 15 for layer sub-rects) in `hitTestTransformHandle`. At the normal **23% working zoom that's only ~2.5 SCREEN-px** of grab target. Live-confirmed with a falloff probe on an isolated glyph: **0&ndash;2 screen-px from a corner hit `se`, but 4px+ returned `rotate`** &mdash; so a slightly-off grab of a scale corner ROTATED instead of scaling.
- **FIX** (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js` `hitTestTransformHandle`; token `spb-corner-grab-20260605f`): enlarged **ONLY the 4 scale corners** to a **zoom-aware constant ~11 screen-px** grab (`rCorner = max(legacy, 11 * canvas.width/clientWidth)`), **capped to 45% of the element's short half-axis** so corner grabs never overlap each other / the edge handles / the move zone on tiny glyphs. Edges (`n/s/e/w`) + the rotate handle keep the legacy radius **on purpose** &mdash; rotate sits ~32px above the top-centre edge, so widening its/the edge grab would swallow the top-middle handle. Corners sit far from rotate, so they're safe to widen.
- **VERIFIED live (after reload, `hasRCorner:true`):** falloff probe now shows the corner grabs out to **~11 screen-px** (`se` at 0/4/8px; was `rotate` at 4px+), while the edge (`rm`) is unchanged (`e` only at 0px). **Money shot:** dispatched a drag from a point **8 screen-px INWARD of a corner** &mdash; pre-fix that returned `move`; now `hitTestTransformHandle`&rarr;`se`, `dragging:'se'`, and it **SCALED** (105% / 82%, rotation stayed 0). An imprecise grab that used to move/rotate now scales, like Photoshop. Test scale reverted via Cancel; livery unchanged; 0 console errors. 3-copy synced; cache-buster bumped.
- **LEFT:** (a) zoom-aware VISUAL handle size + a wider rotate-handle offset so edges can be widened safely too; (b) make isolate zoom IN for small glyphs so handles are big on screen (cleanest Photoshop-like answer); (c) breadth: brush/eraser/lasso/wand/recolor/gradient on a throwaway layer.

### 2026-06-05 (later) &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; owner /loop: FIXED "clicking near a logo moves the whole layer" footgun (drag dead-zone)
- **Transform is now seamless (prior entry, iter1&ndash;5), so moved to BREADTH per owner "cover ALL tools".** Live-tested per-element isolate on non-glyph art (sponsor logos + the big Car&nbsp;Paint body): isolate + HUD-dock + Cancel all work on large elements too (auto zoom-to-fit to the element, Pos&nbsp;1024,1024, revert clean) &mdash; not just small number glyphs.
- **FOUND A REAL FOOTGUN, reproduced LIVE:** with a layer selected (Sponsors) in PICK&nbsp;ITEM, a single click that lands just OFF an isolatable element (a transparent layer pixel) **moved the ENTIRE layer** &mdash; toast "Layer moved" / "Undid: move layer". Exactly the "tools don't work right" class the owner is angry about: try to nudge a logo, the whole layer jumps.
- **ROOT CAUSE** (`paint-booth-3-canvas.js`): mousedown (~L3044) first tries `selectConnectedLayerPixelsAtPoint`; if it returns falsy it falls through to `startLayerDrag`, and `updateLayerDrag` moved the layer **+ pushed undo on the VERY FIRST mousemove** &mdash; so ordinary click-jitter immediately nudged the layer.
- **FIX** (token `spb-layer-drag-deadzone-20260605e`): added a Photoshop-style **drag dead-zone** to `updateLayerDrag` &mdash; no move, no undo-snapshot, no toast until the cursor travels **&gt;5 screen-px** (zoom-independent: `hypot(dx,dy)/sx`, sx = canvas.width/clientWidth). `endLayerDrag` now only announces "Layer moved" if a move actually happened, so a pure click ends silently. Undo snapshot still fires on the first REAL move (preserves Bockwinkel B2 Ctrl+Z restore). 3-copy synced; cache-buster bumped.
- **VERIFIED through the REAL drag functions** (after reload; `hasDeadzone:true` confirmed in the live bundle): a **3-screen-px drag &rarr; layer does NOT move** (`smallMoved:false`); a **10-screen-px drag &rarr; layer moves** (`bigMoved:true`, 44 canvas-px). bbox captured + restored (`restoredOK:true`), spurious test-undo popped with Ctrl+Z &mdash; **livery visually unchanged**. Footgun killed; deliberate drags preserved.
- **LEFT:** continue breadth on other tools (brush / eraser / lasso / wand / recolor / gradient) &mdash; use throwaway layers for destructive ops + undo-verify each; optionally make isolate more forgiving (search a small radius when the exact click pixel is transparent) so near-misses isolate instead of falling through.

Fix: new **`tile`** param in `catalog_blend.blend_registered_specs_float` &mdash; renders each finish at `(h/tile, w/tile)` then **seamless reflect/mirror-tiles** up (no hard seams; works for gradients/radials). `generate.scratch_spec_from_any_paint` auto-applies `PRESET_TILE_BY_ID`. Owner chose *keep tile=1 globally, fix flagged only* &rarr; `PRESET_TILE_OVERRIDE` sets **tile=2 on the 22 `big`-flagged presets only**; the ~100 keeps stay whole-frame. Only `preset_stack` carries the per-preset tile; manual `catalog_stack` picks stay tile=1.
  - **Detail round:** owner re-audited the replacements and flagged **2 as "not detailed enough"** (kintsugi_bloom, volcanic_obsidian) &rarr; swapped for `reactive_matte_shine` (woven cross-hatch) + `living_electric_current` (branching lightning).
- **Lessons (durable):** (a) cultural/illustrative finishes (`vm_`/`rs_`…) don't translate to spec maps &mdash; prefer material families. (b) Pattern scale is **cycles-per-frame**, so the lever for "too big" is **mirror-tiling**, not absolute pixels (preview stays cell-for-cell with the 2048 render). (c) **Quality-score and Laplacian-variance do NOT capture perceptual "detail"** &mdash; Laplacian rewards sparse high-contrast edges (soft glowing dots score high but read plain); pick "more detailed" **visually** from a rendered contact sheet, not by metric.
- 125 live, **19/19 spec_sculpt tests** pass, audit regenerated, 3-copy synced. Verdict-reader: `scripts/spb_spec_sculpt_audit_summary.py`. Next: owner re-audits the 11 replacements + 22 re-tiled finishes (fresh / Submitted cards); if a tiled one still reads too big, bump its `PRESET_TILE_OVERRIDE` to 3.

### 2026-06-01 &mdash; Claude (Opus) &mdash; Spec Sculpt: material diversity redesign
- **Problem (owner-reported):** the Shokk-the-World 24-at-once gallery rendered all looks nearly identical &mdash; "Vantablack" looked like "Show Chrome." Root cause traced: every preset shared **one paint-derived spatial structure** (`_scratch_spec_from_paint`) and diverged only by a **global mrc multiplier**. Measured diversity = mean pairwise RMS **~20/255** (two looks ~1.5 apart).
- **Fix:** new `engine/spec_sculpt/material_profiles.py` &mdash; per-preset **material identity** (baseline M/R/Cc + family spatial texture: uniform/flake/brushed/weave/forged/hammered/hex/crackle/bands/droplets/marble/scales/micrograin + chroma carrier + assertiveness + paint relief). Wired into `generate.py` (`reshape_layer_with_profile` in the stack loop + a post-Viva `apply_character_lock`). **Shared engine left untouched** &mdash; the 1009 monolithics are unaffected (finish-neutral).
- **Result:** mean pairwise distance **~20 &rarr; ~68** (3.4&times;) across the curated 24 *and* the full 121 catalog; clearcoat std **~5 &rarr; ~56**. Deterministic, iron-safe, +~1s at 2048 (batch previews effectively free). Proof harness: `scripts/spb_spec_diversity.py` (contact sheet + metric). Full writeup in **🪄 Spec Sculpt Lab &rarr; Material diversity engine**. `node --check`-clean, all 19 spec_sculpt tests pass, 3-copy synced (new module added to `runtime-sync-manifest.json`).
- **Follow-up (after viewing renders):** (a) killed a faint square *mesh* artifact that the shared Viva NEAREST grids left on **every** preset (even smooth chrome) &mdash; character lock now Gaussian-smooths that residual instead of preserving it; (b) made all geometric textures **frame-relative + ~3&times; finer** via a single `_TEX_DENSITY` knob (2048² covers a whole car body, so thumbnail-small = vehicle-huge), carbon/circuit/perforated/hex finer still, soft `tanh` tows to kill moire. Preview now matches the 2048 render cell-for-cell.
